title: Spreading rational maps from generic points of smooth special fibres
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $E=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Fibres and products mean scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. An open $U\subseteq Y$ of a $T$-scheme is $T$-dense if $U_s$ is dense in $Y_s$ for both $s\in T$. A $T$-rational map is an equivalence class of morphisms on $T$-dense opens, where representatives agree on a $T$-dense open of their common domain. A $T$-birational map is represented by an isomorphism between $T$-dense open subschemes. Let $Z\to T$ be smooth and of finite type and let $V\to Z$ and $W\to Z$ be smooth finite-type morphisms, with $W\to Z$ separated [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $h_E:V_E\to W_E$ be a morphism over $Z_E$. For every generic point $\xi$ of $Z_k$, put $A_\xi=\mathcal O_{Z,\xi}$ and $L_\xi=\operatorname{Frac}(A_\xi)$; these local rings are discrete valuation rings. Suppose the base change of $h_E$ to $L_\xi$ extends to a morphism $D_\xi\to W_{A_\xi}$ over $\operatorname{Spec}A_\xi$, where $D_\xi\subseteq V_{A_\xi}$ is open, contains the generic fibre, and is dense in the special fibre. Then there is a $T$-dense open $D\subseteq V$ containing $V_E$ and a $Z$-morphism $h:D\to W$ extending $h_E$. If $h_E$ is an isomorphism and each local extension is an isomorphism between $\operatorname{Spec}A_\xi$-dense opens, then $h_E$ extends to a $T$-birational map $V\dashrightarrow W$. In this situation, any two $Z$-morphisms from an open subscheme of $V$ to $W$ agreeing on its generic fibre are equal; consequently the extensions on such opens agree on overlaps. Finally, let $R'$ be a discrete valuation ring and $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to T$ a morphism sending the closed point to the closed point and the generic point to the generic point. For any $T$-scheme $X$ and $T$-dense open $U\subseteq X$, the base change $U\times_T\operatorname{Spec}R'$ is $\operatorname{Spec}R'$-dense in $X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}R'$; consequently the base change of a $T$-birational map is $\operatorname{Spec}R'$-birational.

source.place: BLR 2.5 Proposition 5, printed p.58 (PDF p.64), and its local-ring use in 4.3 Proposition 5 and 4.4 Corollary 4, printed pp.108,111 (PDF pp.114,117). Local spreading formulation of those arguments; ordinary generic-fibre uniqueness is included explicitly. Primary scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $R$. Every nonzero element of $R$ is $u\pi^n$ with $u$ a unit by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], so $E=R[1/\pi]$ by the formula $a/(u\pi^n)=(au^{-1})/\pi^n$. The principal-localization and open-base-change results identify $Y_E$ with the open $D(\pi)$ in every $T$-scheme $Y$. Thus intersections with the generic fibre below are actual open subschemes, and inverting $\pi$ commutes with every base change.

The DVR $R$ is Noetherian since every ideal is principal. Finite-type composition and finite-type preservation of Noetherianity show that $Z,V,W$ are Noetherian. Their opens are Noetherian and hence quasi-compact; locally Noetherian schemes are quasi-separated. Smoothness gives local finite presentation, and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes] gives the same for restrictions to opens. Consequently $V_N,W_N$, and every open in either, are of finite presentation over any affine open $N\subset Z$: quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of these morphisms follow from the qcqs permanence lemma. The same holds after base change to $A_\xi$, since stalks are localizations of Noetherian affine coordinate rings and localizations remain Noetherian. The special fibres $Z_k,V_k,W_k$ are Noetherian and have finitely many irreducible components.

For a generic point $\xi$ of $Z_k$, the local ring $A=A_\xi$ is Noetherian by Step 2. Smoothness of $Z\to T$ gives flatness, so multiplication by $\pi$ on $A$ is injective by the torsion-free consequence of flatness over the domain $R$. The special fibre is reduced by the smooth-fibre reducedness lemma. In an affine open of $Z_k$ the point $\xi$ is a minimal prime, and its local ring is the localization there by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]; it is a field by the minimal-prime localization lemma. The fibre-stalk quotient lemma identifies that field with $A/\pi A$. Hence $(\pi)$ is the maximal ideal of $A$. Apply [lem-sbc-regular-principal-prime-localization-dvr] with $H=B=A$ and $g=\pi$: localization of a local ring at the complement of its maximal ideal is itself. This proves that $A$ is a DVR. Step 1 applied to $A$ identifies $A[1/\pi]$ with $L_\xi$; its residue field is $\kappa(\xi)$.

First establish the uniqueness assertion for any open $B\subset V$. The composite $V\to Z\to T$ is smooth, hence flat. At every stalk of $B$, multiplication by $\pi$ is injective by flatness over $R$. It is therefore injective on the coordinate ring of each affine open in $B$: a section annihilated by $\pi$ has zero germ everywhere. By [lem-pc-affine-nonzerodivisor-complement-dense] the restriction $\mathcal O_B\to j_*\mathcal O_{B_E}$ for the quasi-compact inclusion $j:B_E=D(\pi)\to B$ is injective affine-locally and hence on $B$, so $B_E$ is scheme-theoretically dense in $B$ in the sense of [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open]. Two $Z$-morphisms $B\to W$ agreeing on $B_E$ are equal by [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated], since $W\to Z$ is separated. In particular every pair of extensions agreeing with $h_E$ agrees on its entire overlap.

source.place: Tag 07ZU (lemma-effective-Cartier-complement); morphisms.tex Tags 01VA and 01VF; BLR 2.5, schematic density and uniqueness discussion, printed pp.55-57.

proof.text: Smoothness is preserved by base change. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-reduced-dense-pullback] to $V_k\to Z_k$ and to $W_k\to Z_k$, using the reduced locally Noetherian base $Z_k$ from Steps 2-3. Thus each generic point of $V_k$ or $W_k$ maps to a generic point $\xi$ of $Z_k$. A point generic in $V_k$ lying over $\xi$ remains generic in the fibre $V_{\kappa(\xi)}$: a strict generalization there would give a strict generalization in $V_k$. A dense open in a Noetherian scheme contains every generic point of its finitely many components: remove the other components to obtain a neighborhood belonging only to the selected component, and use density there. Therefore each local domain $D_\xi$ contains every generic point of $V_k$ over $\xi$, viewed in this localized closed fibre.

source.place: Tag 034E (lemma-reduced-local-smooth); algebra.tex Tag 00HS (lemma-flat-going-down); BLR 4.3 Proposition 5 proof, printed p.108 (PDF p.114).

proof.text: Fix $\xi$ and an affine neighborhood $N_0\subset Z$ of it. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods], $\operatorname{Spec}A_\xi$ is the inverse limit of its affine open neighborhoods $N\subset N_0$, ordered by reverse inclusion, with affine transitions. Base-changing $V_{N_0}$ gives the inverse system $V_N$ with limit $V_{A_\xi}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-fibre-products]. All stages are qcqs by Step 2. The open $D_\xi$ is quasi-compact by Step 2, so [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] supplies an affine neighborhood $N$ and an open $D_N\subset V_N$ whose pullback is $D_\xi$. This node also identifies $D_\xi$ with the limit of the later opens $D_{N'}=D_N\times_NN'$.

Both $D_N$ and $W_N$ are finitely presented qcqs schemes over $N$ by Step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-arrows-descent] to the given map $D_\xi\to W_{A_\xi}$ over the affine-neighborhood system. After shrinking $N$ it descends to an $N$-morphism $h_N:D_N\to W_N$. Its base change to $A_\xi$ is exactly the supplied local extension, with the specified identification of domains. Regard $D_N$ as an open of $V$ and $h_N$ as a $Z$-morphism to $W$.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), part (2); direct spreading argument underlying BLR 4.3 Proposition 5.

proof.text: It is necessary to arrange equality with the given map on the generic open, rather than merely at $L_\xi$. On $(D_N)_E$, compare $(h_N)_E$ with $h_E|_{(D_N)_E}$ as morphisms to $W_E$ over $Z_E$. Their restrictions to $(D_\xi)_{L_\xi}=V_{L_\xi}$ agree by the local-extension hypothesis. The qcqs affine-transition system $(D_{N'})_E$ has this limit, because fibre products commute with the neighborhood limit and $A_\xi[1/\pi]=L_\xi$. Since $W_E\to Z_E$ is locally of finite type, [lem-weil-pbc-locally-finite-type-limit-map-equality] makes the two maps equal at a later stage. Replace $N$ by that smaller neighborhood. No claim that $D_N$ contains all of $V_E$ is used.

source.place: Tag 01ZC (proposition-characterize-locally-finite-presentation), injectivity part of the finite-type comparison; Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), part (3).

proof.text: Perform Steps 6-8 for each generic $\xi$ of $Z_k$. Define $D=V_E\cup\bigcup_\xi D_N$, an open of $V$ containing $V_E$. The morphisms $h_E$ and $h_N$ agree on all overlaps by Step 4 and Step 8, so [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] gives a morphism $h:D\to W$. Each constituent is over $Z$, hence the glued morphism is over $Z$, as can be checked on this cover. The generic fibre of $D$ is all of $V_E$. Every generic point of $V_k$ is contained in some $D_N$ by Step 5 and the identity $(D_N)_{A_\xi}=D_\xi$. Thus $D_k$ contains the generic points of all components of $V_k$ and is dense. This proves the first extension assertion.

source.place: Tag 01JA (section-glueing-schemes); BLR 4.3 Proposition 5 and 4.4 Corollary 4, printed pp.108,111; explicit local spreading assembly.

proof.text: For the birational assertion, write each supplied local isomorphism as $e_\xi:D_\xi\xrightarrow{\sim}H_\xi$ with $H_\xi\subset W_{A_\xi}$ open and dense in its special fibre. Since $D_\xi$ contains $V_{L_\xi}$ and $e_\xi$ restricts to the isomorphism $h_{L_\xi}$, its image contains $W_{L_\xi}$. Descend both quasi-compact opens by [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] along the same neighborhood system as in Step 6. After a common shrinking, obtain $D_N\subset V_N$ and $H_N\subset W_N$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-arrows-descent] to $e_\xi$ and $e_\xi^{-1}$ to obtain maps $e_N:D_N\to H_N$ and $a_N:H_N\to D_N$ with those exact local pullbacks.

source.place: Tags 01Z4 (lemma-descend-opens) and 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), part (2); BLR 4.3 Proposition 5, birational conclusion.

proof.text: Over $A_\xi$ the composites $a_Ne_N$ and $e_Na_N$ become the respective identities. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-locally-finite-type-limit-map-equality] to the later systems of $D_N$ and $H_N$, with targets these fixed finitely presented $N$-schemes. After a common shrinking both identities hold. Thus $e_N$ is an isomorphism with inverse $a_N$. Apply the same equality lemma to the generic-open systems to arrange $e_N|_{(D_N)_E}=h_E|_{(D_N)_E}$ and $a_N|_{(H_N)_E}=h_E^{-1}|_{(H_N)_E}$, by the argument of Step 8. Equality descent requires no separatedness of its target, so this is valid for the inverse with target $V_E$.

Let $C_1,\ldots,C_r$ be the irreducible components of $Z_k$, with generic points $\xi_i$. In each neighborhood $N_i$ from Steps 10-11, remove $\bigcup_{j\ne i}C_j$, viewed as a closed subset of $Z$ because $Z_k$ is closed. The result still contains $\xi_i$ and may be replaced by an affine neighborhood of $\xi_i$ inside it. Restrict $D_{N_i},H_{N_i},e_{N_i},a_{N_i}$ accordingly. For $i\ne j$, the intersection $N_i\cap N_j$ has empty special fibre, so lies in $Z_E$. Indeed, any point in the special fibre belongs to some $C_t$, and membership in $N_i$ forces $t=i$, whereas membership in $N_j$ forces $t=j$. Localized domains and images at $A_{\xi_i}$ are unchanged.

source.place: Explicit finite-component neighborhood choice for the local spreading argument (agent argument); finiteness established in Step 2.

proof.text: Put $D'=V_E\cup\bigcup_iD_{N_i}$ and $H'=W_E\cup\bigcup_iH_{N_i}$. All maps $e_{N_i}$, together with $h_E$, take values in $H'$. Their inverses take values in $D'$. For distinct indices every domain overlap is over $Z_E$ by Step 12, so the maps agree there by Step 11; overlaps with the generic piece agree for the same reason. Glue both families using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. The two composites are identities because they are identities on every member of the respective open covers, again by this node's uniqueness assertion. Hence $D'\simeq H'$ over $Z$. By Step 5 and the density of the local domains and images, $D'$ and $H'$ contain all generic points of their special fibres; their generic fibres are whole. Thus both are $T$-dense. This represents the claimed $T$-birational map, without assuming $V\to Z$ separated.

source.place: Tag 01JA (section-glueing-schemes); BLR 4.3 Proposition 5, printed p.108, birational extension; explicit simultaneous gluing of inverse maps.

proof.text: For the last assertion, let $t'$ be either point of $T'=\operatorname{Spec}R'$ and let $t$ be its image in $T$. By the two point-image hypotheses these are respectively the generic and closed points. The fibre of $X_{T'}$ at $t'$ is $X_t\times_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(t')$, and likewise for $U$. The projection $p:X_t\times_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(t')\to X_t$ is open by [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open]. If $O$ is any nonempty open of its source, then $p(O)$ is nonempty open and meets the dense open $U_t$. A point in this intersection lifts to a point of $O$ by the meaning of image; that point belongs to $p^{-1}(U_t)$. Thus $p^{-1}(U_t)$ is dense. Apply this at both $t'$. This proves the asserted fibrewise density for arbitrary $X$, without a finite-type hypothesis or a flatness assumption on $X$.

source.place: Tag 0383 (lemma-scheme-over-field-universally-open); BLR 2.5, definition of S-dense opens, printed p.55; elementary open-map density argument.

proof.text: Base-change an isomorphism between $T$-dense open subschemes representing a $T$-birational map. The two base-changed domains are open, the isomorphism and its inverse remain inverse by functoriality of fibre products, and Step 14 makes both opens $T'$-dense. This is a representative of a $T'$-birational map. Equivalence of representatives is preserved too: a $T$-dense common agreement open stays $T'$-dense by Step 14, and the equality of its two maps is preserved by base change.
